<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par135 />a trace of popular language), e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=23|verse=22}}(?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=5|verse=5}}, and (like other indications of the very late origin of the book) very frequently in Ecclesiastes, e.g. 1:16, 2:1, 11, 15, 3:17f. and thirteen other places; in Aramaic, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=5|verse=16}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|c}}
2. Substantival subjects also are somewhat frequently resumed, and thus expressly emphasized, by the insertion of the corresponding separate pronoun of the 3rd person before the predicate is stated, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=12}} ''the woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she'' ({{GHGheb|text=הִיא}}) ''gave me'', &c.; 14:24 ({{GHGheb|text=הֵם}}); 15:4, 24:7, &c.; but {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=14}} after the predicate and subject is equivalent to ''he himself''.<ref>Analogous to this is the resumption of a noun dependent on a preposition, by means of a pronominal suffix united with the same preposition, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=22|verse=18}}, or of an object by means of the {{GHGterm|nota accusativi}} {{GHGheb|text=את}} with suffix, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=15|verse=9}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וְנִמְאֶ֫סֶת}} is certainly to be read), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=13}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|d}}
'''2.''' Not infrequently the separate pronoun serves to give strong emphasis to a suffix of the same person which precedes (or sometimes even to one which follows), whether the suffix be attached to a verb (as accusative) or to a noun or preposition (as genitive). In English such an emphasis on the pronoun can generally be rendered only by laying greater stress upon it, or sometimes by repeating it; cf., on the contrary, the French ''mon livre à moi''. The separate pronoun in such instances is not to be regarded as a ''casus obliquus'' (accusative or genitive), but as the subject of an independent sentence, the predicate of which must in each case be supplied according to the context.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|e}}
Examples of emphasis:—

(''a'') On a {{GHGterm|verbal}} suffix by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָ֫נִי}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=34}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽרֲכֵ֫נִי גַם־אָ֫נִי|translate=bless me, even me also}} (prop. ''bless me, I also'' would be blessed); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=7|verse=5}}; cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=34|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, 20 {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנִי אָ֫נִי}}; by {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָ֫תָּה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=22|verse=19}} (but the text is most probably corrupt).—The separate pronoun ''precedes'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=27}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי}}); 49:8 ({{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה}}, not ''Judah, thou art he whom'', but ''Judah thee, thee thy brethren shall praise!''), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=15}} {{GHGheb|text=גַּם אֲנִי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|f}}
(''b'') On a noun-suffix with a substantive, by means of {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=23|verse=15}}; by {{GHGheb|text=אָ֑תָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶת־דָּֽמְךָ גַּם־אָ֑תָּה|translate=thy blood, even thine}}; by {{GHGheb|text=הוּא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=3}}; by {{GHGheb|text=אֲנַ֫חְנוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=20|verse=42}}, after {{GHGheb|text=שְׁנֵ֫ינוּ}}, but without special stress; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=5|verse=2}} (?); by {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=14|verse=32}}; by {{GHGheb|text=הֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=11}} (without special stress), {{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=9|verse=7}}.—The separate pronoun ''precedes'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=21|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=40|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=28|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=9|verse=11}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתְּ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=23|verse=9}} ({{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=33|verse=17}} ({{GHGheb|text=הֵ֫מָּה}}).—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=89|verse=48}}, where {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}} might be taken as strengthening {{GHGheb|text=חלד}} (equivalent in sense to {{GHGheb|text=חֶלְדִּי}}), we should read {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי}} for {{GHGheb|text=אֲנִי}}, as in verse 51.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|g}}
(''c'') On a suffix united with a preposition, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=24}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּי אֲנִי|translate=upon me, upon me}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לִי... אֲנִי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=35|verse=21}} {{GHGheb|text=לֹא־עָלֶ֫יךָ אַתָּה|translate=not against thee}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=19|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=עָלָיו גַּם הוּא|translate=upon him also}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=כִּי אִתָּנוּ אֲנַ֫חְנוּ|translate=but with us, even us}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Hag|chapter=1|verse=4}} {{GHGheb|text=לָכֶם אַתֶּם|translate=for you yourselves}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=25|verse=14}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּם גַּם־הֵ֫מָּה}}.—The separate pronoun precedes in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=12|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=אָֽנֹכִי... לִי}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה... עָלֶ֫יךָ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=5|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתָּה... מִמְּךָ}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=אַתֶּם עִמָּכֶם}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|135|h}}
The same principle also explains {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=לְשֵׁת גַּם־הוּא|translate=to Seth, to him also}} (not {{GHGheb|text=גַּם־לוֹ}}); cf. 10:21, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=35|verse=34}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=22}}.
